verdictReason: All 8 functional requirements, 3 non-functional requirements and 5 constraints are accurately covered. One MEDIUM completeness issue requests explicit coverage of existing authoring writes and cancellation/abandonment settlement in the all-guard audit and race tests. No HIGH issue; proposal scope and core native immutable revision approach are sound.

issues.description: The complete freshness guarantee is concrete for manual save, compile, confirm and execute, but the existing Steps/context/configuration save contract and background cancellation/abandonment settlement remain implicit. The ordered page Save starts through the existing authoring endpoint without explicitly requiring the code/mode/hash expectations there; AT-6 names failure/timeout but not cancellation or the abandonment sweeper. Current StudioService authoring writes compare only source/configuration and CompileStateService.sweepAbandoned selects by status/time, so these existing writers need explicit inclusion in the proposed audit. This is specification precision, not evidence that the proposed architecture permits a bypass.
issues.suggestion: Add a concise writer/outcome guard matrix covering existing authoring/Steps/context/config writes with expected/current F, manual save/mode switch, preparation capture, success/failure/deadline/cancellation/abandonment, confirmation, readiness and acceptance. Distinguish request-supplied expected F from the current immutable capture checked by background workers. Extend AT-6 to show an older cancellation/sweeper cannot clear a newer manual candidate/request or revoke unchanged confirmed readiness. This does not require a new user cancellation feature.

nextAction: Return to @pm spec-write for CRIT-1 precision revision, preserve critique-1.json, then run independent critique_2 required by COMPLEX19. This verdict concerns specification quality only, not implementation completion, product adoption or release authorization.
